(Defs.lean:110-113) matches `.imp _ .bot` unconditionally (no exclusion for a `.box` antecedent), so tryAllPropRules's negPos/negNeg arms are ALWAYS applicable first for the diamondPos/diamondNeg shapes (verified computationally via lean_run_code, both directions, `rfl`-provable generically over the box's body). modalApplyOne's diamondPos/diamondNeg match arms are consequently dead code, never reached at runtime -- T(dia phi)@w is instead decoded by negPos into F(box(not phi))@w, which fires boxNeg (2-step composition achieving the same semantics). Only boxNeg's `.neg, .box _` shape is never intercepted by any propositional rule pattern (`.box` is a distinct top-level constructor from every prop-rule pattern's `.imp`-headed shape). This does NOT weaken the outDeg<=Sf bound -- it makes the bound's supporting invariant actually TRUE (the original two-shape version would have been FALSE, since a T-diamond-shaped formula firing via negPos is a non-edge-creating step that would still have inflated the naive filtered count).
